--- title: "13 — Tracking a drifting DARM parameter" description: "The DARM loop's calibration parameters drift, forcing continuous re-measurement. On the coupled reduced-quad plant, inject known slow variations into an actuation strength κ(t) and into the SRC detuning δ(t) — which splits the cavity pole into a complex pair — and recover both with Lataire–Pintelon basis fits on leakage-free P&S snapshots, within honest Cramér–Rao bands and with resolvability proven by a computed bound." image: thumbnails/13.svg categories: [calibration, closed-loop, DARM, time-varying] freeze: true --- ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} ## What you'll learn - Why a *drifting* plant is a system-ID problem, not a re-measurement chore. - Recovering a time-varying actuation strength **κ(t)** from leakage-free snapshots, with a real CRB. - Tracking the **SRC detuning δ(t)** — the *new* physics of the coupled plant, where the cavity pole splits into a complex pair — from the Pcal FRF, independent of the κ drift. - Proving each drift is **resolvable** with a computed bound — not eyeballing the plot. ::: The [DARM calibration page](08-darm-calibration.qmd) recovers the loop's sensing, actuation, and response at **one instant**. But the reason DARM calibration is the slowest recurring LIGO measurement is that those parameters **drift** — the optical gain, the coupled-cavity pole, and the actuation strengths wander over minutes to hours, so the calibration is re-measured again and again. This page treats that drift head-on: as a slowly time-varying system to *identify*, not a nuisance to average away. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## The plant and the scope This runs on the **new coupled DARM plant** — the M0-damped reduced-QUAD hierarchical actuation (M0 / PUM / ESD) with coupled detuned-cavity sensing, where the SRC detuning splits the cavity pole into a complex pair (the same twin as [example 08](08-darm-calibration.qmd)). The drifts are **known, smooth deterministic** profiles: one on the ESD actuation strength κ(t), one on the SRC detuning δ(t). The goal is to show the machinery **tracks each drift within its error bar**. Still deferred to a later round: a stochastic/GP wander, several parameters drifting *jointly*, and the one-shot (rather than two-step) Lataire–Pintelon fit. Rendered with `freeze: true`. ::: ::: {#85e24df3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Setup — import the presentation glue"} import sys, pathlib _p = pathlib.Path.cwd() for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]: if (_c / "docs" / "darm_tv_demo.py").exists() and str(_c / "docs") not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c / "docs")) if (_c / "darm_tv_demo.py").exists() and str(_c) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c)) import numpy as np import darm_tv_demo as dd from IPython.display import display ``` ::: ## The idea: locally stationary snapshots The plant drifts far more slowly than one measurement record (an hour-scale drift versus a ~16 s record), so within any single record it is **locally stationary** — the Pintelon–Schoukens picture of a linear model around a slowly-moving operating point. That licenses a two-step estimator: 1. **Snapshot.** At a sequence of times, take one leakage-free periodic-multisine measurement and recover the instantaneous actuation strength with **Pcal as the ruler**. Because the sensing `C` cancels in the stage-to-Pcal ratio, each snapshot is *immune to sensing drift* and carries an honest per-estimate σ. 2. **Basis fit.** Fit `κ(t) = Σ cₖ bₖ(t)` in a time-basis (Legendre) to the snapshot series by weighted least squares — a Lataire–Pintelon basis expansion in two-step form. The coefficient covariance **is** the Cramér–Rao bound on the drift curve κ(t) and its rate. We drift the **ESD (TST) stage** — the one whose strength really wanders in an interferometer, as charge builds on the reaction mass — with a 5 %, hour-scale profile, on the coupled reduced-quad plant (the ruler `H_stage/H_pcal = κ_i·D_i·N_i` recovers κ through the M0-damped compliance and the nested-offload distribution). ::: {#a4f519f0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Run the campaign — snapshot the drift, fit κ(t)"} c = dd.campaign(seed=777) ``` ::: ## Tracking the drift The injected truth, the per-record snapshots with their error bars, and the recovered κ(t) with its CRB band: ::: {#f4d85cde .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="κ(t): injected truth, snapshots ± σ, LP fit ± CRB"} dd.drift_fig(c) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The fit rides straight through the snapshots and follows the injected drift — a 5 % excursion resolved cleanly, even though each single snapshot only pins κ to about a percent. ## Is the recovery honest? A curve through points is easy; a curve that knows its own uncertainty is the point. The recovery residual (recovered − truth) stays inside the ±σ Cramér–Rao band — the error bar neither collapses (which would be fabricated confidence) nor balloons (which would be uselessly conservative): ::: {#4b080b56 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Tracking error vs the CRB band"} dd.tracking_error_fig(c) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## The feasibility gate: is the drift resolvable? Before calling a drift "trackable" or "buried in noise," compute the bound. The tracking σ from the fit is far below the injected drift amplitude, so the drift is genuinely **resolved**, not noise — and the local-stationarity approximation costs a fraction of a percent, well under the per-snapshot error: ::: {#f4bc1862 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Resolvability — a computed bound, not an eyeball"} display(dd.resolvability_table(c)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Feasibility gate — the injected drift is resolvable (a computed bound, not an eyeball)** | feasibility quantity | value | note | | --- | --- | --- | | injected drift amplitude | 0.0500 | 5% of κ | | per-snapshot σ_κ (median) | 0.0005 | 0.05% of κ | | tracking σ_κ (LP fit, median) | 0.0002 | 0.02% of κ | | resolve ratio = amp / tracking σ | 224× | ≫ 1 ⇒ drift resolved, not noise | | local-stationarity error | 0.22% | record ÷ drift timescale — the approximation cost | ::: ::: The resolve ratio is a knob, not a limit: more periods per snapshot, more snapshots, or a stronger drive all buy it down further — the same Fisher levers as everywhere else in the pipeline. ## The new physics: a drifting SRC detuning δ(t) The coupled plant lets us track the drift that the old single-pole twin could not represent: the **SRC detuning δ**. As the SRC error point wanders around its slightly-detuned operating point, the cavity pole moves — splitting toward a complex pair — and the sensing shape changes with it. δ is a *sensing* parameter, so it does **not** cancel in the κ ruler; instead it is recovered from the **Pcal FRF shape** (`C_meas = H_pcal·(1+G)`), which makes the δ snapshot independent of the κ drift — the two compose into a joint κ(t), δ(t) picture. We drift δ by 5 % around a 5° operating point: ::: {#d91fcdba .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Snapshot the drifting SRC detuning δ(t) from the Pcal FRF, fit δ(t)"} cd = dd.campaign_delta(seed=778) dd.delta_drift_fig(cd) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#2e00e224 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="δ(t) resolvability — a computed bound"} display(dd.delta_resolvability_table(cd)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **SRC-detuning drift is resolvable — δ tracked from the Pcal FRF, independent of the κ drift (the two snapshots compose).** | feasibility quantity | value | note | | --- | --- | --- | | injected drift amplitude | 0.2500° | 5% of δ | | per-snapshot σ_δ (median) | 0.0035° | 0.07% of δ | | tracking σ_δ (LP fit, median) | 0.0015° | 0.03% of δ | | resolve ratio = amp / tracking σ | 167× | ≫ 1 ⇒ drift resolved, not noise | | local-stationarity error | 0.22% | record ÷ drift timescale | ::: ::: The detuning is recovered to a hundredth of a degree per snapshot — the coupled-cavity split leaves a strong high-frequency signature in `C`, so δ is well-identified even at this small detuning. Note the separation of concerns: κ comes from the stage/Pcal *ratio* (immune to sensing drift), δ from the Pcal *shape* (immune to actuation drift), so a real interferometer's simultaneous κ- and δ-drift are tracked by two independent snapshots on the same records. ## Honest gaps The drifts here are *known, deterministic* profiles tracked *one parameter at a time*. Still to come: a stochastic (GP) wander in place of the smooth profile, a **joint** fit of κ(t) and δ(t) (and the other TDCFs) drifting together rather than independently, and the one-shot (rather than two-step) Lataire–Pintelon estimator. What this page establishes is the foundation they build on: on the coupled reduced-quad plant, the machinery **tracks both an actuation strength and the SRC detuning within a Cramér–Rao bound**, and the "can we track it?" question gets a numeric answer — see `notes/darm-calibration-via-pns.md`.
